Lost memories, regrets, love, and longing yet its not presented in his usual shoegaze-y, hazy way but in something so bleak. Making this a sequel to In The Mood For Love was so smart cuz of how much of a juxtaposition this is to that. I mean ITMFL is the worlds greatest love story to some, the pinnacle of eroticism without physical touch, eternal longing and heartache, and sure the latter half is obviously present as Mr Chow grows, but this movie relies on its tone being sex-filled, grey, and apathetic. Also kind of the most tragic of his films cuz of how alone Mr Chow truly is and how he seeks distraction thru sex and reliving past loves with new women, and putting all his truths and feelings into his writing absentmindedly. " Maybe the next one darling, maybe the next one." Cronenberg's masterpiece. Put it simply its a masterpiece on all fronts. Perfect from its script to its direction to its score to its aesthetic to its acting to its tone. Sensual in a hazy numb way from start to finish. Dreary and existential in the horniest way possible. Just pure human loneliness and connection, the innate urge to feel the same as others have felt before u. The movie equivalent of going on a spiral on reddit to see if anyone else is feeling ur symptoms and finding that someone has, but with a psychosexual metal vehicular twist. The reshaping of the human body with modern technology as Vaughnn says how modern technology creates new fears, wants, desires in us all. New intimate feelings created solely from technology. Cars are inherently sexual. The roar of an engine, the angles and curves in chrome, the possibility and freedom and liberation of a car is sexy and sensual and ughh theres a restrictiveness to a car. The tug of a seatbelt, the lull of traffic, that when all that is released it feels like a climax. The way the car breathes after a crash, the steam that rises, the stillness of the moment, a metallic explosion of energy its hot stuff idk! The repetitive nature of the movie eats, controlling the unpredictability of life and death thru car crashes and release and feeling a sort of power thru these acts. Looking for different ways to plug the hole of want u feel. movie is too good and flew by on this rewatch i could have watches like 2 more hours of this.

Wowowow im not a documentary person at all, frankly ive never even voluntarily put one on even tho ive always been intrigued but what a way to dive into my documentary foray. This film was brilliant idk how to describe it other than it just being brilliant. It's presented in this vignettes collected throughout Johnson's career so each clip is a tiny, ephemeral punch of emotion and beauty and natural and reality and all together its just so stunningly impactful. Some of vignettes are taken from her work on survivors of wars and massacres and the locations these events took place but they arent filmed with this sense of vouyerism, but rather just feel so human. Theres no false sense of heaviness that filmmakers attempt to add to their sets, but rather it just is what it is. A swimming pool used for executions is just a swimming pool, a mountain thats a mass grave site is one of the most beautiful things in the film, the theme park in afghanistan, the farms of post war bosnia, its just all filmed with so much care. Johnson just knows the power of subtlety and holding back and knows how to build emotion with how she placed these clips. It has a hypnotism to it, its so real, cried twice but also im feeling more hopeful to be alive than ever feeling so incredibly human. The abortion clinic one, the post match boxing, the nigerian hospital, the soldier refusing to get deployed again, Johnson's own mother and her struggle with alzheimers god it was all great, love love loved this

Possible 5 alert guys holy shit? Um just one of the most symbolically dense screenplays ever? Every line in that final amazing scene with Giammatti and Pattinson feels incredibly impactful and important. That last scene is just so good like two greats doing the best work Ive seen from both, two characters both so victimized by the world and their own undoing that they turn to violence, despair, surrender. You can just take so much from this. At the beginning i was thinking it was exploring the concept of being a young ingenue, peaking early and the anxiety of being a has been with time. But as it went on what really stood out was Eric's strive for perfection and the constant masking of his childhood fear of dying. Eric's father dying quickly and unexpectedly from cancer scarred him so now everyday he's getting checkups by doctors, stressing over his asymmetrical prostate. "We have minutes to live." he says. Constant rumination on how time is running from him. "Time is a thing that grows scarcer everyday." That's why he's become this billionaire playboy, he's trying to outbid time. " Money makes time." It's like the journey for a perfect, stressfree life is a fallacy and only leads to pain, dissatisfaction , and anxiety no matter how many daily checkups, or meet ins with a chief of philosophy u have. Everything is crumbling, the world is dissatisfied and disillusioned, rats roam the streets, nothing is right, nothing is how it showed be, yet Eric is still betting on the norm instead of thinking outside it. That's why he lost his fortune in a day, that's why he has constant anxiety and masks it with sex, screens, and limousines. Perfect performance by Pattinson just captures eric's bravado, youth, anxiety and sadness so well. When he is told that his friend is dead u can see him imagine his own premature death. When the barber admonishes him for no having protection u can see him shrink into a little boy being told that hes doing something wrong. Its like u can tell eric carries a lot of childhood fear over his father dying so quick, yet he's also so full of contradiction and bravado and masculinity that he enters a room where he knows he might possibly die in. The way both Eric and Benno look for salvation in other people and then get let down when they don't meet their standards- " I wanted you to save me." Im also just a huge sucker for 2000's artificiality in films i love the schlock of mid 2000's to 2010's cgi i love when directors play into how fake it looks and turn it surrealist and i love when characters speak like book protagonists and not real people lmfao

in my usual annoying fashion i came into this with a hypercritical lens but icl Nolan absolutely washed every preconceived notion i had regarding basically everything abt the film. From Odysseus' characterization, which i found as both an excellent modern adaptation and also extremely faithful to the source material, to the visuals to the acting to the pacing to themes, i really think theres a pantheon of perfect films out there and The Odyssey is a new addition to it. I think this is a perfect film. Honestly my favorite aspect of this is how mind candy themes are. Odysseus, literature's first hero (Gilgamesh aside) being the ancient equivalent to what Oppenheimer was in the 50's, the predecessor to violence, the mastermind of original sin. The First Story, The First Man, the narrative of all narratives that most of western literature has based their tales, behaviors, and beliefs off of being translated to one of violence, deceit, lies, greed, and treachery was genius. The story that started it all isn't one of honor or forgiveness or empathy, but one made up of rage and rot. There's a deep sadness to this film, what have we become, what started it all, the gods have turned away or actually the gods are rooting for this. We have forsaken them, they want to see it burn so they can rebuild it all, and YET AND YET once it is rebuilt, it will happen again. Violence must get its feed, blood must be spilt, guts must be drawn. The Odyssey to Oppenheimer to Tenet, a reversed trilogy of sorts which is so Tenet, all exploring the cause-and-effect and consequence of human action. Past, future, present, now, then, violence does not care, humans have not changed just simply forgotten and then reborn. And yet, im not leaving completely bleak. There's always those fools who wish for a better tomorrow and Nolan is one of them, he knows we are in a moment of collapse as a society and through these 3 movies he seems to be reflecting on the cause of it all, but there's a sense of hopeful gravitas to this. Really quickly wanna add what i think is the part of this film that's gonna stick with me the most which is how fucking ugly this movie looked (not derogatory). The garish quality of the horse to the mountains to the sea to the castles, a story that should be so grand and epic and glorifying the spoils of war and the battles we have all known and that have informed practically every form of media since are all framed so disgusting and revolting and heartless and grave. There's heartlessness to this film that's is both deliciously enticing and bleak to watch. That talking to the dead scene.....peak stuff....

But for some reason i feel underwhelmed bc of it? I think the first hour is absolutely amazing stuff, the video game shit, the modals, the new morpheus, Neo's memories subjugated to being replayed, his love story being bastardized to the masses, and forced to live in his own private hell were something will forever be slightly wrong. It's great stuff i fucking love when the matrix is smaller scale like this, when it's exploring reality and fiction and memory and choice vs when it's action blockbuster. The scenes of past movies being used as video game footage was genius, The Matrix itself being discussed as a touchstone of film, as a film that's been dissected, reexamined, reclaimed, stolen, all of the above was great and then it's even cooler when u relay it back to Wachowski herself well kinda sad actually bc studios will only fund a film like this bc of its legacy yet will not give her the funds to create more genre defining work post Matrix. The world's she built do not belong to her any longer, yet she still is making one last ditch effort at ownership again. I wish we stayed in this space for more of the film.
